facts.raw_span: asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
involvement of the upper respiratory tract, causing palatal perforation and stridor, necessitating a tracheostomy a year ago
no history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring measuring 2 × 1 to 8 × 7 cm on the face, arm, and thighs
saddle nose deformity, perforation of the hard palate, and necrotic plaques on the ear with destruction of ear cartilage
cervical lymphadenopathy: multiple, nontender, discrete nodes, ranging from 1.5 to 2 cm without surface changes
anemia (hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL)
normal kidney function test
normal liver function test
infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)
pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species

concepts.why: The presence of pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, and parakeratosis in the skin biopsy, along with the characteristic fungal skin culture, are diagnostic of Chromoblastomycosis.
The fungal skin culture showing black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species, along with the histopathological findings, support the diagnosis of Exophiala infection.
The presence of pigmented hyphae in the skin biopsy and the characteristic fungal skin culture are consistent with Phaeohyphomycosis, a dematiaceous fungal infection.
It explains the involvement of the upper respiratory tract and destruction of ear cartilage.

rationales.F01: Erythematous scaly plaques are common in chromoblastomycosis and phaeohyphomycosis.
rationales.F02: Upper respiratory tract involvement is more characteristic of Exophiala infection and phaeohyphomycosis.
rationales.F05: Saddle nose deformity and perforation of the hard palate are more characteristic of Exophiala infection and phaeohyphomycosis.
rationales.F10: Infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts is characteristic of chromoblastomycosis, Exophiala infection, and phaeohyphomycosis.
rationales.F11: Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes are characteristic of chromoblastomycosis, Exophiala infection, and phaeohyphomycosis.
rationales.F12: Fungal skin culture showing black yeastlike colonies is characteristic of Exophiala infection.

frontier_selector.rationale: Exophiala infection is supported by the fungal skin culture showing black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species, which is a specific finding that outweighs other non-specific evidence.
